Marubeni Corporation.desc: A Japanese general trading and investment company, founded in 1858 and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, dealing in food and agriculture, metals and minerals, energy and chemicals, power and infrastructure, finance and leasing, and aerospace. The group had 52,658 employees as of 31 March 2026.

HP Gauff Ingenieure.desc: A German engineering and consulting firm in Nuremberg that plans and manages water, sewage, energy, district heating, road, traffic and airport projects, and also does construction management and procurement. It is registered as GAUFF GmbH & Co. Engineering KG, founded in 1988, with about 70 staff at the Nuremberg head office.

sources.title: GAUFF GmbH & Co. Engineering KG company record
sources.publisher: Bayern International / Key to Bavaria (Bavarian state business database)

Ondeo (Suez).desc: Ondeo was the brand the French utility group Suez gave its water businesses in March 2001, covering Lyonnaise des Eaux, Nalco and Degremont. At the launch the water activities were put at 9.1 billion euros of revenue for 2000, with 60,000 staff in 130 countries. Suez, with shares on the New York Stock Exchange, had group revenues of 39.6 billion euros in 2003 and completed the sale of Ondeo Nalco on 4 November 2003.

Benpres (Lopez group).desc: A Philippine investment holding company incorporated in 1993 by the Lopez family, set up to hold investments in broadcasting and cable, telecoms, power and banking; at the end of 2009 it held 57 percent of ABS-CBN Broadcasting and 42 percent of First Philippine Holdings. The Securities and Exchange Commission approved its renaming to Lopez Holdings Corporation in 2010.

sources.title: SEC okays Benpres name change to Lopez Holdings

Vivendi.desc: A French group that began as a water company: Compagnie Generale des Eaux was renamed Vivendi in 1998, and in December 2000 it merged with Seagram and Canal Plus to form Vivendi Universal, with shares traded on Euronext Paris and depositary shares on the New York Stock Exchange. Revenues were 25.5 billion euros in 2003. Its environmental arm, Vivendi Environnement, was floated in Paris in 2000 and renamed Veolia Environnement in 2003.

Anglian Water (AWG Group).desc: Anglian Water Services supplies water and runs water recycling networks for nearly seven million customers; it is the main operating company of Anglian Water Group, which is registered in Jersey and tax resident in the UK. AWG was a listed group until investors bought it in 2006.

Sociedad Comercial del Plata (Soldati gr.desc: An Argentine holding company founded in 1927, with stakes in building materials, fuel distribution and lubricants, food, oil and gas production and rail freight. Its shares trade on the Buenos Aires stock exchange and are in the MerVal index, and group sales were about 476 million US dollars in 2025.

Motor Columbus (LAMI consortium).desc: A Swiss electricity holding company based in Baden, listed on the SWX Swiss Exchange, whose main asset was a 58.5 percent stake in the power company Atel; its shareholders at the end of 2005 were UBS (55.6 percent), EDF International (20 percent) and EOS Holding (15.5 percent). Group net sales were 8.58 billion Swiss francs with about 8,377 staff in 2005; it was merged into Atel in 2006 and the name disappeared.

Acres International.desc: An employee-owned Canadian consulting engineering firm in Oakville, Ontario, with about 800 staff, working on power, water resources and oil and gas projects. It agreed to be bought by the engineering group Hatch in July 2004 and was renamed Hatch Acres in 2005.

LTA Ltd..desc: A South African civil, mechanical and electrical engineering contractor, formed in 1965 from the merger of James Thompson, Lewis Construction, Steeledale Reinforcing and Amco, and listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange. Its work is now carried on in the Aveng group, whose construction business trades as Aveng Grinaker-LTA.

Campenon Bernard.desc: A French civil engineering and construction firm founded in 1920 by Edme Campenon and Andre Bernard, building bridges, dams, tunnels and metro lines. Compagnie Generale des Eaux took control in 1984 and the firm merged into SGE in 1988; SGE became VINCI in 2000.

sources.title: Campenon Bernard
sources.publisher: Structurae (International Database for Civil and Structural Engineering)

EDF (via EDF Nam Theun Holding).desc: France's main electricity company, generating and supplying power with a large nuclear fleet; it had about 120 GW of installed capacity and 41.1 million customers in 2025. The French state completed a buy-out of the shares and became sole shareholder on 26 May 2023; EDF Nam Theun Holding is the group vehicle holding its stake in the Nam Theun 2 project.

sources.title: The French State becomes the sole shareholder of EDF again

Electricity Generating Public Company (E.desc: A Thai power holding company set up in 1992 by the state utility EGAT as part of opening electricity generation to private investors; it earns its income from dividends from power plant subsidiaries and joint ventures in Thailand, the Asia-Pacific and North America. It became a public company in 1994 and has traded on the Stock Exchange of Thailand since January 1995.

sources.title: Corporate Profile and History
sources.publisher: Electricity Generating Public Company Limited (EGCO Group)

Lao Holding State Enterprise.desc: A Laotian state-owned company set up in February 2005 to hold the Lao government's shareholdings in power projects, including 25 percent of the Nam Theun 2 Power Company.

Fortis Bank.desc: The Belgian banking arm of the Fortis financial group. It reported a loss of 20.6 billion euros for 2008; the Belgian state took it over in the 2008 bail-out of the group and was in the course of selling a 75 percent stake to the French group BNP Paribas when the result was announced in April 2009.

sources.title: Fortis Bank reveals EUR 20.6bn loss for 2008

American Metal Climax (copper subsidiari.desc: A US mining, metals and energy company based in New York, formed in 1957 by merging American Metal Company (founded 1887) with Climax Molybdenum; it later traded as AMAX Inc. Its African copper interests were the Roan Antelope and Mufulira mines, held partly through Rhodesian (later Roan) Selection Trust, of which Zambia took 51 percent in 1970.

Bujagali Energy Limited.desc: A Ugandan independent power producer that runs the 250 MW Bujagali hydropower plant on the Victoria Nile, commissioned in 2012 and supplying up to about 31 percent of Uganda's effective capacity. Its shareholders are TotalEnergies, Bujagali Holdings Power Company (an affiliate of the Aga Khan Fund for Economic Development) and the Government of Uganda.

Industrial Promotion Services (Aga Khan.desc: The infrastructure and industrial development arm of the Aga Khan Fund for Economic Development, an international development agency; it invests in and runs businesses in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania and DR Congo among others. As of 2012 its power assets included a 288 MW gas plant in Cote d'Ivoire and a 75 MW diesel plant in Kenya.

sources.title: Bujagali Energy Successfully Delivering First 50MW of Clean Energy to the Ugandan Electricity Grid

Sithe Global.desc: A power plant developer, Sithe Global Power LLC, which develops, finances, builds and operates power stations, with a pipeline of about 5,000 MW of projects in the Philippines, India, Africa and the Middle East. Funds managed by the private equity firm Blackstone bought 80 percent in 2005 and raised the holding to 99 percent in 2011.

sources.title: Bujagali Energy Successfully Delivering First 50MW of Clean Energy to the Ugandan Electricity Grid

AES Nile Power.desc: A Ugandan project subsidiary of the US independent power producer AES Corporation of Arlington, Virginia, set up to build, own and operate a 200 MW hydropower station at Bujagali costing about 580 million US dollars. AES withdrew from the project in August 2003 and wrote off about 75 million dollars.

sources.title: Update: AES pulls out of $580 million Uganda dam project

KN Construction Company (KNCC).note: Blanked on fact-check. The only source, a 1998 Human Rights Watch memorandum, was opened: it calls KNCC 'a regular and major contractee of NTPC' and places it doing ash dike work near Mitihini village, but says nothing about the company's business, sector, ownership or size, and does not use the term 'Singrauli complex'. No company website, Indian company register entry or news report describing the firm could be found. What the memorandum does say is the firm's role in the case, which the card already shows.

Tchad Oil Transportation Company (TOTCO).desc: A pipeline company that manages the 178 km Chadian section of the Chad-Cameroon oil export pipeline. ExxonMobil held an interest in it which Savannah Energy agreed to buy in December 2022; Chad then used a right of pre-emption and took the assets bought from ExxonMobil, TOTCO among them, into state ownership (reported 2023).

sources.title: Chad upset over irregularities in management of pipeline with Cameroon

Montana Exploradora de Guatemala.desc: A Guatemalan gold mining company, registered in 1996, that ran the Marlin mine in San Marcos from 2005; the mine produced 202,200 ounces of gold in 2013 and stopped producing on 31 May 2017. It was a wholly owned subsidiary of Glamis Gold, which merged into the Canadian miner Goldcorp in 2006.

sources.title: Goldcorp's Marlin mine: a decade of operations and controversy in Guatemala
Montana Exploradora de Guatemala, S.A. (1996-present)
sources.publisher: Legal Cultures of the Subsoil, Institute of Latin American Studies, University of London

Grupo GOLAN.note: Blanked on fact-check: no usable source. Searches for Grupo Golan in connection with Guatemala and the Marlin mine return only a user-edited wiki and campaign material; no company site, company register entry or news report describing the firm could be opened. The brief rules out a user-edited wiki as the only source.

RANSA.desc: A Peruvian logistics company, Ransa Comercial S.A.C., based in Callao, founded in 1939 as a cotton storage business and now running warehousing, customs bonded and cold storage, cargo handling and road transport, including hazardous materials. It has more than 7,000 employees, and the private equity firm H.I.G. Capital became majority shareholder of Grupo Ransa in 2021.

sources.title: Ransa Comercial S.A.C. pre-operational certification audit report

Coastal Gujarat Power Limited (CGPL).desc: An Indian power company, wholly owned by Tata Power, that built and ran the 4,000 MW supercritical coal-fired Mundra Ultra Mega Power Project in Gujarat. The National Company Law Tribunal approved its amalgamation into Tata Power by an order dated 31 March 2022, so it is no longer a separate company.

sources.title: NCLT approves amalgamation of Coastal Gujarat Power with Tata Power

Tata Power.desc: An Indian electricity company that generates, trades, transmits and distributes power, with thermal, hydro, wind and solar plants. It had 16,716 MW of generation capacity and more than 13.1 million distribution customers in the 2025-26 financial year, and total income of 669.92 billion rupees in 2024-25.

sources.title: Tata Power reports profit of Rs 47.75 billion in 2024-25

Oyu Tolgoi LLC.desc: The Mongolian company that holds the Oyu Tolgoi copper and gold mine in Umnugovi province, with open-pit mining from 2011 and underground production from March 2023. Rio Tinto holds 66 percent and manages the operation, and the Mongolian state holds 34 percent through Erdenes Oyu Tolgoi; the mine is expected to produce up to about 500,000 tonnes of copper a year between 2028 and 2036.

Turquoise Hill Resources.desc: A Canadian mining company whose shares were listed on the Toronto and New York stock exchanges as TRQ and whose main asset was its interest in the Oyu Tolgoi copper and gold mine in Mongolia. Rio Tinto bought the shares it did not already own for about 3.1 billion US dollars and the company became a wholly owned Rio Tinto subsidiary on 15 December 2022; its shares ceased trading.

sources.title: Rio Tinto completes acquisition of Turquoise Hill

Erdenes Oyu Tolgoi LLC.desc: A Mongolian state-owned company, a wholly owned subsidiary of the state holding company Erdenes Mongol LLC, set up in 2011 to hold the government's 34 percent shareholding in Oyu Tolgoi LLC.

Compagnie des Bauxites de Guinée (CBG).desc: A Guinean bauxite mining company that owns and works the Sangaredi mine in the Boke region, the largest bauxite mine in Guinea. The Government of Guinea holds 49 percent and Halco Mining 51 percent, held through Halco's subsidiary Boke Investment Company; the mine produced 13.7 million tonnes of bauxite in 2019.

Halco Mining Inc..desc: A holding company that owns 51 percent of Compagnie des Bauxites de Guinee through its subsidiary Boke Investment Company. It is a joint venture of the mining groups Alcoa and Rio Tinto, with 45 percent each, and the privately owned Dadco group with 10 percent.

Alcoa.desc: A US aluminium company incorporated in Delaware that mines bauxite, refines alumina and smelts and casts aluminium, with 26 operating sites in nine countries. Its shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange, and it had about 13,900 employees at the end of 2024.

sources.title: Alcoa Corporation Form 10-K for fiscal year 2024

Dadco.desc: A privately owned investment, manufacturing and trading group in the aluminium industry, part of a group whose founding company dates from 1915, and a leading European supplier of alumina-based products. Its head office is in St Peter Port, Guernsey, and its Aluminium Oxid Stade refinery in Lower Saxony, Germany, can make over one million tonnes of alumina a year; it is a shareholder in Halco Mining.

Freeport-McMoRan.desc: A US copper, gold and molybdenum mining company incorporated in Delaware in 1987 and listed on the New York Stock Exchange as FCX, with headquarters in Phoenix, Arizona. Its main operations are the Grasberg district in Indonesia, Morenci in Arizona and Cerro Verde in Peru.

Desarrollos Energéticos S.A. (DESA).desc: A Honduran hydropower developer behind the Agua Zarca project, planned at 21.3 MW with about 98.8 GWh a year. Its executive president, Roberto David Castillo Mejia, was arrested in 2018 over the murder of Berta Caceres.

sources.title: Desarrollos Energeticos executive arrested in murder of anti-hydro activist in Honduras

Siemens.desc: A German technology company founded in Berlin in 1847, making automation, digitalisation and electrification equipment and software for industry, buildings, power grids and transport. Group revenue was 78.9 billion euros in the 2025 financial year.

sources.title: Earnings Release and Financial Results Q4 FY 2025

Voith.desc: A family-owned German technology company with its headquarters in Heidenheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, making hydropower plants and equipment, drive systems and papermaking machinery. It reported sales of 5.2 billion euros and about 22,000 employees for the 2023/24 financial year.

Oil Palm Uganda Ltd (OPUL).desc: A Ugandan oil palm plantation company that signed an agreement with the Ugandan government to run an integrated palm oil project in Kalangala district, part of the state Vegetable Oil Development Project backed by IFAD and the World Bank. It sits within Bidco Uganda, a joint venture of Bidco Africa and Wilmar International, which the Uganda Investment Authority licensed on 10 September 2003 for a planned 30,000 hectares in Kalangala and Masaka.

Bidco Oil Refineries.desc: A family-run Kenyan manufacturer of edible oils, fats, soaps and personal care goods, started by the Shah family with a small soap factory at Thika in 1985, which added edible oils in 1991. It had more than 40 brands sold in 16 countries and reported turnover above 500 million US dollars in 2013.

sources.title: Be persistent, never give up: The story of Vimal Shah and Bidco
sources.publisher: How we made it in Africa

Industrial and Commercial Bank of China.desc: A Chinese state-owned commercial bank, founded in 1984, offering lending, deposits and other banking services. It has been listed since 2006, with A-shares in mainland China and H-shares in Hong Kong, and it had nearly 49 trillion yuan of total assets and about 170 million personal customers at the end of 2024.

sources.title: 2024 Annual Results Presentation
sources.publisher: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited

Hoang Anh Gia Lai (HAGL).desc: A Vietnamese agriculture company whose main businesses are fruit, mostly bananas and durians for export, and pig farming; it is chaired by Doan Nguyen Duc and listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange. Net revenue was 5,694 billion dong (about 227 million US dollars) in 2024.

sources.title: Vietnam's agri major Hoang Anh Gia Lai sees profit down 41% in 2024

Dragon Capital Group.desc: An independent investment and asset management firm founded in Ho Chi Minh City in 1994, managing listed equity, fixed income, clean technology and property funds focused on Vietnam, with offices in Hanoi, Hong Kong, Bangkok and Bath. It launched the Vietnam Enterprise Investments Limited (VEIL) fund in 1995 and listed it on the London Stock Exchange main market in 2016.

Thames Water.desc: A British water and sewerage utility that supplies drinking water and treats wastewater for about 16 million customers in London and the Thames Valley. The operating company, Thames Water Utilities Limited, was incorporated on 1 April 1989 and has its registered office in Reading, England.

Vitens.desc: A Dutch drinking water company that abstracts groundwater, treats it at 93 production sites and distributes it through about 48,000 km of mains to around 6 million people and businesses across five provinces. It delivered 352.9 million cubic metres of water and had 1,910 permanent staff in 2025, and is owned by government bodies as shareholders.

Rand Water.desc: A South African water board established under the Water Services Act of 1997 and classified as a national government business enterprise, selling bulk drinking water to municipalities, mines and industry in Gauteng and parts of neighbouring provinces. Its shareholder is the national government through the Minister of Water and Sanitation; it supplied an average of 4,642 megalitres a day and employed 3,437 staff in 2021-22.

sources.title: Integrated Annual Report 2021/22
sources.publisher: Rand Water (tabled in the South African Parliament)

Empresa Eléctrica Pangue S.A..desc: A Chilean electricity company set up for the Pangue hydroelectric project on the upper Biobio river. The International Finance Corporation held 2.5 percent of its equity from October 1993 and committed a 170 million US dollar loan, and sold the stake in July 2002.

sources.title: Chile: Empresa Electrica Pangue S.A.-01 / Upper Bio-Bio Watershed

Hidroeléctrica Santa Rita S.A..desc: A Guatemalan company formed to build the 23 MW Santa Rita hydroelectric plant on the Rio Icbolay in Alta Verapaz, registered as the project participant for a UN Clean Development Mechanism project. It was part-owned by the Latin Renewables Infrastructure Fund, which later said it would not develop the project.

sources.title: Guatemala: Investigation of Indigenous Peoples Concerns Regarding Hydropower Project
Santa Rita Hydroelectric Plant, CDM project record
sources.publisher: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change

Real Infrastructure Capital Partners.desc: The firm that raised and sponsors the Latin Renewables Infrastructure Fund, which invests in renewable power generation in Latin America, with a focus on Central America. The fund reached a first close of about 50 million US dollars in July 2012 against a target of 150 to 200 million.

sources.title: Real Infrastructure Capital Partners Reaches First Close for Latin Renewables Infrastructure Fund

PT Asiatic Persada.desc: An Indonesian oil palm plantation company in Jambi province, Sumatra, holding a 20,000-hectare permit acquired in 1986. The agribusiness group Wilmar International took over the company in 2006 and sold it in April 2013 to Prima Fortune International and PT Agro Mandiri Semesta.

sources.title: Palm oil deal undermines efforts to resolve 25-year conflict in Sumatra

PT Agro Mandiri Semesta (Ganda Group).desc: An Indonesian oil palm company and a unit of the Ganda Group, owned by Ganda Sitorus, brother of Wilmar International's founder Martua Sitorus.

sources.title: Palm oil deal undermines efforts to resolve 25-year conflict in Sumatra

China State Construction Engineering Cor.desc: A Chinese state-owned construction and property group based in Beijing, working on housing, infrastructure, property development and design in China and abroad. Fortune ranked it 17th in its Global 500 list, with revenue of about 290 billion US dollars and 370,272 employees.

sources.title: China State Construction Engineering, Fortune Global 500

EDF International (Électricité de France.desc: A wholly owned subsidiary of the French electricity group EDF that holds and manages the group's investments in energy companies outside France, including EDF Energy, Edison, Luminus and EDF Inc. The net book value of its shareholdings was 23.3 billion euros at the end of 2022.

Nachtigal Hydropower Company (NHPC).desc: The Cameroonian project company for the 420 MW Nachtigal hydropower plant on the Sanaga river, built for about 1.2 billion euros with a 35-year operating concession. At the signing of the final agreements on 8 November 2018 its shareholders were EDF (40 percent), the IFC (30 percent) and the Republic of Cameroon (30 percent).

sources.title: EDF, IFC and the Republic of Cameroon sign final and binding agreements for the construction of the Nachtigal hydroelectric dam in Cameroon
EDF, IFC, Republic of Cameroon sign agreements to build 420-MW Nachtigal hydropower plant

Mota-Engil Engenharia e Construção Áfric.desc: The African arm of Mota-Engil, a Portuguese engineering and construction group with about 70 years in the business and offices in 24 countries, 15 of them in Africa, including Uganda. The parent company's shares are listed in Lisbon under the ticker EGL.

Ruhore Company Limited.note: Blanked on fact-check: no usable source. The Daily Monitor report on the Tororo-Kamdini road quarry dispute was opened and does not name Ruhore at all; it names Mota-Engil and otherwise refers to an unnamed company and an unnamed local third party. No company website, Uganda Registration Services Bureau entry or other report naming the firm could be found.

Societe Zhengwei Technique Cooperation S.desc: A Chinese construction company operating in the Democratic Republic of Congo. In 2020 it was awarded a contract, shared with the Belgian group Putman-Malcon&TSE, to drill 28 water boreholes in five provinces.

sources.title: DRC: SZTC and Putman-Malcon&TSE to drill 28 water wells in Grand Kasai

China Railway Seventh Group (CRSG).desc: A Chinese state-held construction company, part of China Railway Group Limited and founded by China Railway Engineering Corporation, which builds roads, railways, bridges, tunnels, buildings and hydroelectric works and makes concrete components.

sources.title: China Railway Seventh (7th) Group Co. Ltd (CRSG) organisation profile

THDC India Ltd.desc: An Indian state-controlled power company incorporated in July 1988, building and running hydro, thermal, wind and solar plants and a coal mine, with 3,918 MW of installed capacity. Since a 2020 share sale it is 74.5 percent owned by NTPC Limited and 25.5 percent by the Government of Uttar Pradesh.

Cairo Electricity Production Company (CE.desc: An Egyptian state electricity generator, a subsidiary of the Egyptian Electricity Holding Company. It owns and operates the 1,500 MW Giza North combined-cycle gas power plant, which runs mainly on natural gas with light diesel oil as backup.
